summary: The real-time desk lead (Bill Williams) runs the Portland real-time desk's standing procedures as a stream of one-off emails to the shift group. These cover Enpower deal entry, swaps, cut handling, hourly generator checkouts, customer finals in CAPS or FSP, and transmission scheduling, and some have to be re-sent because traders do not follow them. The fix is a single maintained Real-Time Desk Procedures checklist, organised by topic and reviewed at the start of every shift, plus a short change-notice template, so the lead edits one document instead of re-sending instructions. The main benefit is fewer repeated reminders and fewer missed steps that cause penalties, disputes or complaints from counterparties.

current_workflow.step: A rule or procedure change comes from outside the desk (a CAISO/FERC change, a request from volume management, a CAPS outage, a forwarded idea), and the desk lead forwards it to the shift group with his own instructions on top.

The desk lead emails step-by-step Enpower procedures for particular situations, such as swaps through the swap function, deal #146517 for PGE transmission, and Colstrip cuts with index buys, a BPA wheel, linked deals and a flat check in real time position manager.

Positions and dispatch instructions that only apply for a while (EPE lending shorts by book, Sundance 3 and 4 dispatch for Enron Canada with phone numbers and the dispatch log) go out as separate emails for certain dates.
current_workflow.who: real-time desk lead / Kate Symes (deal details)

current_workflow.step: Shift traders carry out the instructions during their shift: they call CAISO for outages, call Grays Harbor and Frontier every hour and report actuals to BPA, sign off the hour in the services book, and handle cuts using the attached cut sheet.
When a step is missed or forgotten, the lead re-sends a reminder or escalates after a counterparty complains (BPA service complaint, schedule changes not called in, cut notes not copied to him).

stall_points.description: Instructions get lost in inboxes, so the same content is re-sent instead of being looked up in one place.
stall_points.quote: Ryan sent this email out once already, here it is again.

stall_points.description: Standing rules are not followed between reminders, so the lead has to email the shift group again about the same rule.
stall_points.quote: These schedule changes must be called in.  Just a reminder.

stall_points.description: The distribution rules for EES sheets and cut notes are not consistently applied, so the lead misses information and has to send a correction.
stall_points.quote: I should be copied on the EES sheets, and any cut notes to volume managament, the services desk, or other traders.

stall_points.description: An hourly checkout procedure was not done consistently, and the desk found out from a counterparty escalation that threatened the services business.
stall_points.quote: Warren explained to me the necessity and importance of calling in and reporting the actual amount of energy generated by Grays Harbor and Frontier EVERY hour.

stall_points.description: Deal entry done the wrong way in Enpower (annuities instead of swaps) has caused downstream disputes that dragged on for months.
stall_points.quote: Swaps have caused disputes that have dragged on for months in the past, so call me with any questions.

stall_points.description: A nightly deadline set by volume management is passed on only as a forwarded email, with nothing in a shift routine to make sure it gets done.
stall_points.quote: Volume management needs us to create customer finals by 3AM each night in CAPS or FSP.

solution.approach: Gather the standing instructions now spread across the lead's emails into one Real-Time Desk Procedures checklist, kept as a single shared document that the shift.portland group can reach. It has fixed sections: Start-of-shift checks, Hourly duties (generator checkouts and services book sign-off), Enpower deal entry (swaps, transmission deals, specific deal numbers), Cuts (the existing cut sheet plus the Colstrip steps), CAISO rules (price cap, outage calls, wheeling fee components), Nightly deadlines (customer finals by 3AM in CAPS or FSP), Distribution list rules, and a Temporary instructions page with start and end dates (EPE lending, Sundance dispatch, CAPS outages). Every trader goes through the Start-of-shift section and the Temporary instructions page at the start of each shift. When something changes, the lead edits the matching section and sends a short change-notice email from a fixed template that names the section and the change, instead of rewriting the whole procedure. Questions keep going to the lead by phone, as they do today, and any answer that becomes a rule is added to the checklist.
solution.trigger: The start of each shift, when the incoming trader reviews the checklist, and any new rule or procedure change that reaches the desk lead (a CAISO/FERC change, a volume management request, a system outage, a new trade arrangement), which prompts an edit to the checklist and a change notice.
inputs: standing instruction emails from the desk lead (Enpower procedures, CAISO rules, cut handling, checkouts)
the existing cut procedures sheet attached to the CUTS email
deadlines from volume management (customer finals by 3AM)
temporary arrangements with dates (EPE lending books and deal numbers from Kate, Sundance dispatch window)
outputs: the Real-Time Desk Procedures checklist for shift traders
a start-of-shift checklist section with the hourly and nightly duties
short change-notice emails to the shift group naming the section that changed
components: Real-Time Desk Procedures checklist document (sectioned by topic)
Temporary instructions page with start and end dates
change-notice email template (section, what changed, effective date, owner)
shift sign-off line confirming the checklist was reviewed

implementation_steps: Go through the lead's past instruction emails to the shift group and pull every standing rule into a draft, grouped into the fixed sections (Start-of-shift, Hourly duties, Enpower deal entry, Cuts, CAISO rules, Nightly deadlines, Distribution rules, Temporary instructions).
Put the existing cut procedures sheet and the Colstrip cut steps under Cuts, and write the swap, PGE transmission deal and EPE lending entry rules as numbered Enpower steps.

Write the start-of-shift checklist with the time-bound duties: hourly Grays Harbor and Frontier checkouts reported to BPA and signed off in the services book, CAISO outage calls, customer finals by 3AM in CAPS or FSP, and who gets copied on EES sheets and cut notes.
Save the document where every shift trader can reach it, and link to it from the shift.portland group's standing materials.
Write the change-notice email template, and agree that the lead updates the document first and then sends the notice, instead of a free-form procedure email.
Go through the checklist with the group at the next real-time meeting and have each trader confirm in the shift sign-off that they reviewed it.
Review the Temporary instructions page weekly and remove entries whose end date has passed.
stays_manual: Deciding trading strategy and when a rule applies (buying over the price cap for reliability, dec bids or buy-backs with generators), because these are market judgments the lead makes.
The phone calls themselves (to CAISO, BPA, the generators and the power pool), because the evidence says they must be called in until the generators are automatically metered.
Handling unusual cuts or outages that the checklist does not cover, which still go to the lead or Les by phone.
Workplace conduct issues such as after-hours behavior, which the lead handles directly and which do not belong in a procedures checklist.
risks: The checklist goes stale if the lead keeps sending free-form emails. Mitigate by making the change-notice template the only route and checking at the weekly meeting that the document matches recent notices.
Traders may skip reading it. Mitigate with the shift sign-off line and by keeping the start-of-shift section to one page.
The evidence comes from one mailbox (williams-w3) and does not show where shared desk documents are kept or whether a shared drive exists. Confirm the location with the desk before rollout.

Phone numbers, passwords and deal numbers in the instructions change, and some (for example the power pool login) should not go in a widely shared document. Keep credentials out and put a review date on contact details.

At the computed value of $76 a month ($912 a year), the case rests on fewer penalties, disputes and counterparty complaints rather than on email time saved. Those avoided costs are not quantified in the evidence.
success_metric: Number of reminder or re-sent instruction emails from the desk lead to the shift group per month, plus the number of counterparty escalations about missed hourly checkouts or outage calls, compared before and after rollout.
